newsitem.title: UK: HORSE RACING-FALLON HOT FAVOURITE TO TOP ROYAL ASCOT.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-FALLON HOT FAVOURITE TO TOP ROYAL ASCOT.

text.p: Kieren Fallon, revelling in his new job as Henry Cecil's stable jockey, is 4-5 odds on favourite to finish top rider at the four-day Royal Ascot meeting starting on Tuesday.
With two classic winners already under his belt this season, Fallon is riding at the peak of his powers and with up to 20 top-class partners at Ascot he looks set for at least four or five winners.
Cecil caused a surprise when he plucked Fallon from the northern England circuit but the 32-year-old Irishman has already begun to repay the faith shown in him.

Leading three-year-old filly Sleepytime won the 1,000 Guineas and Fallon followed up in the Epsom Oaks with a highly effective performance on hot favourite Reams of Verse, urging her home in a power-packed finish.
Fallon leads the jockeys' table with 71 winners, more than 15 clear of Frankie Dettori and Pat Eddery. A first championship looks a good bet and Ascot can boot him further along the way.

Sleepytime appears to be one of his bankers in Wednesday's Coronation Stakes, while last year's champion filly Bosra Sham looks good for the Prince of Wales's Stakes on Tuesday. Lady Carla, winner of last year's Oaks, should be another Fallon winner on Friday in the Hardwicke Stakes.
Dettori, whose finest hour came on the Ascot racecourse last September when he rode all seven winners in an afternoon, is going through a lean patch by his standards.

The Godolphin set-up of Sheikh Mohammed, Dettori's main winner-machine, has yet to hit form and Classic Cliche, one of the Godolphin standard-bearers, is still not certain to defend his crown in Thursday's Ascot Gold Cup. The colt has failed to impress fully in recent training. A decision will be made on Wednesday.
Dettori is suspended for the final day on Friday and bookmakers rate him 7-1 to finish top dog at Ascot, behind French champion Olivier Peslier (11-2) and big rival Eddery (6-1).
Eddery's Irish compatriot Michael Kinane, Royal Ascot champion for the last three years, is 8-1 to make it four in succession.

Top American jockey Gary Stevens, who narrowly missed out on the U.S. Triple Crown when Silver Charm was just beaten in the Belmont Stakes earlier this month, rides at the royal meeting for the first time. His best chance may be on the sprinter Almaty in Friday's King's Stand Stakes.

Off the track it will be the usual mixture of high fashion, high attendances and high spirits, fuelled by, among other things, the 50,000 bottles of champagne expected to be served at the 100 bars round the course.
Mindful of the disruption caused by a bomb threat at this year's Grand National, extra security will be in force.

Racecourse director Douglas Erskine-Crum said: "Given the fact there is no IRA (Irish Republican Army) ceasefire, we are obviously taking all the necessary security precautions for an event of our size and profile."
